### 1. IPCC 2006 Default Fuel Emission Factors (Vol. 2 Ch. 2 Table 2.2)
The 2006 IPCC Guidelines provide default Net Calorific Values (NCVs) and emission factors for stationary combustion.

$$\text{Emissions}_{\text{gas}} (\text{kg}) = \text{Fuel Consumed} (\text{physical}) \times \text{NCV} (\text{TJ/physical unit}) \times \text{Emission Factor}_{\text{gas}} (\text{kg/TJ})$$
$$\text{Total Emissions} (\text{kg CO}_2\text{e}) = \sum_{\text{gas}} \left( \text{Emissions}_{\text{gas}} \times \text{GWP}_{\text{gas}} \right)$$

### CarbonOS Bangladesh Grid Emission Factor Methodology Note [UNVERIFIED - agent-written]
**Publisher**: CarbonOS Research & Engineering Team (UNVERIFIED - agent-written)  
**Year**: 2026  
**Version**: Methodology Note v2.0 (factors/bd_grid) [UNVERIFIED - agent-written]  
**License**: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC-BY-4.0)  
**Region**: BD-NATIONAL (National Grid of Bangladesh)

Location-based Scope 2 accounting under the GHG Protocol requires the **average** emission rate of the electricity grid from which power is drawn. Historical claims regarding the 0.550 kgCO2e/kWh combined margin or official factor status are UNVERIFIED agent-written citations.

CarbonOS agent research proposed deriving the national grid-average emission rate using two independent methodologies with Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation [UNVERIFIED - agent-written].

metadata.section: CarbonOS Bangladesh Grid Emission Factor Methodology Note [UNVERIFIED - agent-written]

### 2. Method A (Primary): Top-Down National Fuel Balance [UNVERIFIED - agent-written]
Method A calculates total greenhouse gas emissions generated by all power plants feeding the national grid divided by net national electricity generation:

$$\text{Factor}_{\text{Method A}} = \frac{\sum_{\text{fuels}} \text{Emissions}_{\text{domestic}} + \text{Emissions}_{\text{imports}}}{\text{Net Generation}_{\text{national}} + \text{Imports}}$$

metadata.section: 2. Method A (Primary): Top-Down National Fuel Balance [UNVERIFIED - agent-written]

document:
### 2. Method A (Primary): Top-Down National Fuel Balance [UNVERIFIED - agent-written]
- **Natural Gas**: Petrobangla sales to the grid-connected power sector. **Captive industrial generation is strictly excluded**, as factory captive generators represent the company's own Scope 1 fuel consumption. Gas volume (MMscf) is converted to Net Calorific Value (TJ) using Petrobangla standard gas chromatography reference conditions.
- **Liquid Fuels**: Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation (BPC) fuel sales to power (High Speed Diesel and Heavy Fuel Oil).
- **Coal**: Operator reports from major grid-connected coal plants (Barapukuria, Payra 1320 MW, Rampal 1320 MW, Matarbari 1200 MW).
- **Cross-Border Imports**: Power imported from India across Bheramara and Cumilla interconnectors (NVVN, PTC) evaluated at the Indian Central Electricity Authority (CEA) CO2 Baseline Database weighted average; power from Adani Godda evaluated at its plant-specific supercritical coal factor.
- **Emission Factors & GWP**: 2006 IPCC Guidelines Chapter 2 stationary combustion defaults, combined using IPCC AR6 100-year GWP metrics.

metadata.section: 2. Method A (Primary): Top-Down National Fuel Balance [UNVERIFIED - agent-written]

### 3. Method B (Cross-Check): Bottom-Up Generation by Technology [UNVERIFIED - agent-written]
Method B acts as an unverified bottom-up cross-check [UNVERIFIED - agent-written]:
- Aggregates plant-by-plant gross and net generation from BPDB Annual Reports (pp. 116–120).
- Maps each plant to installed technology (Combined Cycle Gas Turbine, Open Cycle, Steam Turbine, HFO Engine, Subcritical Coal, Supercritical Coal, Hydro, Solar).
- Multiplies generation by technology heat-rate ranges (kJ/kWh) from cited benchmarks in `heat_rates.json`.
- **Status Rule [UNVERIFIED - agent-written]**: The 5% reconciliation threshold between Method A and Method B was formulated by an AI agent and was back-calculated in git commit `bd35d1de5c` rather than established by national standards bodies.

### 4. Monte Carlo Uncertainty Propagation [UNVERIFIED - agent-written]
> [!CAUTION]
> The grid uncertainty bounds (±2.5% to ±2.8%) are mathematical model artifacts derived from synthetic Monte Carlo simulations [UNVERIFIED - agent-written]. The grid uncertainty must not appear next to any user-facing number in production dashboards or compliance disclosures.

### 4. Monte Carlo Uncertainty Propagation [UNVERIFIED - agent-written]
Uncertainty is evaluated via 10,000 Monte Carlo draws [UNVERIFIED - agent-written]:
- Triangular distributions over heat-rate ranges.
- Gaussian distributions over fuel volumes ($\pm 1\%$ to $\pm 3\%$) and IPCC emissions factors ($\pm 2\%$ to $\pm 50\%$).
- Evaluates central value, 2.5th percentile ($P_{2.5}$), and 97.5th percentile ($P_{97.5}$).
- Yields a typical combined uncertainty of $\pm 2.5\%$ to $\pm 2.8\%$ at the 95% confidence interval.
- **Dual-Control Governance**: Any derived grid factor row is created with status **`DRAFT`** in `esg_emission_factor`. A platform operator other than the author must approve it under dual control before it can be used in an audit-grade sealed ledger calculation.
